stemBlocks.value: In triangle PQR, angle QPR = 62 degrees, angle PQR = 90 degrees and PR = 11 cm. Calculate (i) the size of angle PRQ and (ii) the length of side RQ.
Think first: The right angle sits at Q, so PR is the hypotenuse and the whole triangle can be solved with the basic ratios.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p268-q03 from workbook page 268.

solutionSteps.instruction: Use the angle sum of the triangle.

contentBlocks.value: The right angle is at Q, so the hypotenuse is the side facing it, which is PR = 11 cm.

solutionSteps.instruction: Decide which ratio links RQ to PR.

contentBlocks.value: RQ is opposite the 62 degree angle at P, so sin 62 = RQ / PR.

strategyBlocks.value: Subtract the two known angles from 180 degrees for part (i), then use the sine ratio with the hypotenuse PR to find the side opposite the 62 degree angle.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) angle PRQ = 28 degrees  (ii) RQ = 9.71 cm (3 s.f.)

whyThisWorks.value: In a right-angled triangle the hypotenuse is always opposite the right angle, and sine relates the hypotenuse to the side opposite a chosen acute angle. Because the two acute angles of a right-angled triangle add to 90 degrees, finding one immediately gives the other, and you can then choose whichever ratio uses the length you already have.

commonErrors.misconception: Treating RQ as the hypotenuse and dividing by sin 62 instead of multiplying.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Treating RQ as the hypotenuse and dividing by sin 62 instead of multiplying.

commonErrors.misconception: Using the 28 degree angle with the sine ratio for RQ, which gives PQ instead.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using the 28 degree angle with the sine ratio for RQ, which gives PQ instead.

commonErrors.misconception: Leaving the calculator in radian mode.

examTip.value: Mark the hypotenuse first, then label the other two sides opposite and adjacent relative to the angle you are using. The correct ratio then chooses itself.
